items.title: Joe Robichaux Interview, 1959-03-19
items.q: And he told Celestad's band that he had this number and anything they could do with it, you know, they could have it.

ctx.x: Yeah, it's the same thing. You see that was a tune, I think it was Feynman's son was going up to Tulane. And it was his number. And he told Celestad's band that he had this number and anything they could do with it, you know, they could have it. And so John Porter, the bass player, he was hunting and he wrote the lead of it down. And saying he gave them the words. And they began to play it because Celestad and Ridgely band was, they were together then. Yeah. And so finally he wrote it, they wrote it down and they…
Yeah, they didn't know who to pay it to I guess.
